summary.en: Staff officer, royalist, and from 1936 dictator of Greece under the Fourth of August regime. His refusal of the Italian ultimatum on 28 October 1940 took Greece into the Second World War. He died three months before the German invasion.

body_html.en:
Metaxas trained at the Prussian war academy and was the ablest planner of the Balkan War campaigns. He opposed the Asia Minor expedition on military grounds, and was proved right. With the king's consent he suspended parliament in August 1936 and ruled by decree, borrowing the outward forms of fascism without its expansionism.

When Italy delivered its ultimatum in the early hours of 28 October 1940 he rejected it, and the Greek army drove the invaders back into Albania over the following weeks. He died of illness in January 1941, leaving no one able to hold the state together when the Germans came in April.

sources.title: Inside Hitler's Greece: The Experience of Occupation, 1941-44
sources.author: Mark Mazower

title.en: The Italian Invasion and the Albanian Front
